text: When working with APIs, you typically send HTTP requests to a server to get or send data. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy for both computers and humans to read. Before making requests, you often need authentication, usually an API key, to prove who you are. Once you have access, it's important to be aware of rate limits—these restrictions control how many requests you can make in a certain time period. If you exceed them, the API may temporarily block you. Finally, always handle errors gracefully. This means checking the response status and writing code that deals with problems like network failures or invalid input, so your app doesn't crash unexpectedly.
